clue.text: Question for our time? Right! Time to name song at No 1 in the '40s

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era of dating
an age is a long period of time
an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: No 1 read as the number one letter of the word No, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A quiz host asks which song topped the charts during the 1940s.
explanation.walkthrough: The '40s looks like a decade of pop history, but the answer describes a person aged forty to forty-nine.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of that description is aged between forty and forty-nine years, from Latin quadrageni, forty each.

clue.text: Vital part of fruit production outside model town in Germany

indicators.note: the fruit word goes outside, wrapping around the other pieces

parts.note: a quince is a hard yellow pear-shaped fruit
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so model gives T
Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr

explanation.surface: Something essential to fruit growing happens outside a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' sits as a link, helping the surface read as fruit farming.
explanation.definitionFit: The essence or most vital, purest element of something is its quintessence.

clue.text: The Third Man, last of three by tree

parts.note: Abel was the third man in Genesis, after Adam and Cain

indicators.note: signals taking only the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A reference to the film The Third Man, filmed beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The Third Man is Carol Reed's film, but here it is the third human in the Bible: Adam, then his sons Cain and Abel.
explanation.definitionFit: The abele is the white poplar, a kind of tree with silvery leaves.

clue.text: Strange tale, relic of old Italian lace

indicators.note: something strange is out of its usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd story is told about a relic of antique Italian lacework.
explanation.definitionFit: Reticella is a needle lace from Renaissance Italy, an early form of needlepoint.

clue.text: To follow up with broadcast is a boon

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
to send a signal is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Doing a follow-up broadcast turns out to be a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something welcome and timely, as though sent from heaven, is a godsend, a blessing or boon.

clue.text: Hundred thousand taken in after tax, that's characteristic of a smart outfit

indicators.note: the hundred-thousand letters are taken inside the after-tax word

parts.note: net pay is what remains after tax
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
K stands for thousand, as in 10K
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: Someone takes home a large salary after tax, signalling sharp tailoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Hundred thousand looks like one amount but gives two letters, C and K.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie worn round the neck is the typical feature of a smart suit.

clue.text: Cold in space, we're told

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard rather than read, so a soundalike is used

parts.note: room means space, as in no room to move

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is cold out in space.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold here is the illness, not low temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery discharge from nose or eyes, so it stands for a head cold.

clue.text: Timon, I say, is disposed to hate

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Timon of Athens is described as inclined to hate.
explanation.walkthrough: Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope, so the surface is true to the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Animosity is strong dislike or hostility, close to hatred.

clue.text: Awkward number not starting exercises

indicators.note: not starting means the number word loses its opening letter

parts.note: nine is a number
PT is physical training, school exercises

explanation.surface: An ungainly figure struggles to begin a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking skill, which is awkward.

clue.text: Salesman with je ne sais quoi after a month is worn out

indicators.note: after puts the salesman and his allure behind the month

parts.note: Dec. is December
a rep is a sales representative
it means sex appeal or indefinable charm

explanation.surface: A salesman with charisma is exhausted after a month on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrepit means weakened by age or use, so worn out.

clue.text: A cabbage, I do need room to view the ever-changing scene

parts.note: kale is a kind of cabbage
taken as written
scope means room or space, as in room to manoeuvre

explanation.surface: A cabbage needs space for viewing a constantly shifting scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a kaleidoscope is a constantly shifting pattern or sequence of events.

clue.text: Electra cast as a tart?

indicators.note: cast means thrown or moulded anew, so the letters are reset

explanation.surface: An actress is cast as Electra, a fallen woman perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Tart looks like an insult about the casting; it is the pudding, the question mark signalling a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle tart is a classic British pudding, so the syrup names a kind of tart.

clue.text: Grave old lady half gone on fundraiser

parts.note: a tomb is a grave

indicators.note: only the first half of the lady word remains

explanation.surface: An elderly lady half-collapses on a gravestone at a charity event.
explanation.definitionFit: A tombola is a raffle drum or lottery held at fetes to raise money.

clue.text: Reel of rejected fingerprints

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: loops are a common fingerprint pattern

explanation.surface: Police reject a whole film reel of fingerprints as evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool is a cylinder on which thread or film is wound, a reel.

clue.text: Many players may be found in the porch, estranged

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A group of musicians loiter, alienated, on a porch.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental musicians.

clue.text: Equip with oil power to activate slide, I see

indicators.note: activate means set in motion, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Someone converts a machine to oil and sees how to set its slide moving.
explanation.definitionFit: To dieselise is to fit an engine or railway for diesel oil fuel.

clue.text: Drawing copied on this: note one animal man left out

parts.note: E is a musical note
I is the Roman numeral one
a dog is an animal

indicators.note: out means omitted, so the left letter is taken from the man's name

parts.note: Ralph is a man's name

explanation.surface: A note says one animal has been drawn but the man left out.
explanation.definitionFit: An eidograph is an instrument used for copying drawings at a different scale.

clue.text: Onions first eaten by prince in bed on board

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word after it
on board means aboard, inside the ship letters

parts.note: on board ship is between SS, a steamship

indicators.note: the prince goes in the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V

explanation.surface: Onions are eaten first by a prince in his bunk on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Eschalot is an old spelling of shallot, a small mild onion.

clue.text: It enhances the flavour of duck — a daughter of Lear would have none

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, so O
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters
none is zero, O

explanation.surface: A herb that seasons duck; a daughter of King Lear would refuse it.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb used to season food, such as pizza.

clue.text: Press soldiers to be upstanding gentlemen in Italy

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: to iron clothes is to press them
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Journalists urge soldiers to behave as honourable gentlemen in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Press looks like newspapers; it is the verb to iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Signori is Italian for gentlemen or sirs, plural of signore.

clue.text: Nymph in ironic poster

parts.note: dry humour is ironic
an ad, advertisement, can be a poster

explanation.surface: A wood nymph appears in a poster with a wry message.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph in Greek myth.

clue.text: Church keeps lists free from impurities

indicators.note: keeps means holds within, so the church letters surround the list word

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ship lists or leans to one side

explanation.surface: A church keeps lists of names to purge its rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: To cleanse is to make clean, ridding something of impurities.

clue.text: Greek character is taken to tea by the scruff of the neck

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A Greek is dragged off to tea by the scruff of his neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The nucha is the anatomical term for the nape, the back of the neck.

clue.text: One-night stand with heartless girl points to something that may be catching

parts.note: a gig is a single musical engagement

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle letters of the word

parts.note: taken as written before its middle goes
E and S are compass points

explanation.surface: A fling with a cold-hearted girl suggests something contagious.
explanation.walkthrough: One-night stand looks romantic; it is a single concert booking.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is said to be infectious, so the giggles may be caught from others.

clue.text: Learning about one French river

indicators.note: about means around, so the learning word surrounds the one

parts.note: lore is traditional learning
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Learning about a single river in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, flowing to the Atlantic.

clue.text: Disconnected notes coming from old censor following jazzmen about

indicators.note: following places the censor after the musicians
about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: cats is jazz slang for musicians
Cato the Elder was a famous Roman censor

explanation.surface: Notes come from an ancient censor chasing jazz players.
explanation.walkthrough: Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor, a moral overseer.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato notes are played short and detached from each other.

clue.text: Ignoring every other aim, sing to a friend

indicators.note: skip alternate letters, keeping the first, third and so on

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their aims and sings to a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, used informally in English.

clue.text: One has ice cream served for savoury

indicators.note: served up means presented in a new form, so letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone serves ice cream in place of a savoury course.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a baked pasta dish, a savoury rather than a sweet.
